claim: A generic terminal-cost refinement lane fixes the learned policy's first-terminal collapse. Generation one finds a 147-tick terminal route. After the shared replay refit, all four generation-two seeds compare the 147-tick incumbent with the nearest untried parameterization of the same controller path, discover the 130-tick terminal route, and retain it. This proves later learned generations improve route cost, but does not satisfy the full learned-treatment gate because 130 only ties the best equal-budget structured baseline and does not beat the authenticated 125-tick incumbent.

implementation.method: Preserve the exploit control and reserve one learned batch lane for the closest state-local untried action in the best terminal action's structural family. Reactive controllers expose typed button pulse period, phase, and mask parameters plus a digest of the button-free base controller. Refinement holds the base controller identity fixed and varies only typed overlay parameters.

bindings.terminal: authenticated F_SP103 to F_SP104 load-zone commit

negative_control.finding: Without a base-controller identity parameter, the refinement lane varied both path geometry and roll timing and selected route sequence 01. This run did not improve 147. The fail-closed comparison motivated the button-free controller digest used by the corrected treatment.

third_generation_followup.finding: All four third-generation workers compared the next closest available parameter value with the 130-tick incumbent. Period 18 reached the terminal in 152 ticks, so the learned treatment correctly retained period 20. The finite route catalog exposes only periods 16, 18, 20, 22, and 24; the next bottleneck is candidate support, because the learner cannot evaluate adjacent values such as 19 or 21.
